findings.finding: Nordic DIY demand improved through Q3. Byggmax (published 2026-10-20, the day before Salix) reported Q3 like-for-like sales +5.1% (Q2: +1.4%) and operating profit of SEK 292m (258), and Clas Ohlson reported September organic growth of 12% and May-September of 11%. That supports Salix's Home & Fittings arm (sales of SEK 404m in Q2, about 30% of the group), whose DIY-related segments the CEO called 'gradually strengthened' in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Only one prior listed print (Q2, 2026-07-16): +2.9% on the day on 1,337m sales and adj. EBITA +51%, after -4.3% the session before; the stock then drifted from 67 to about 59 over three months.
findings.original_quote: Koncernens jämförbara försäljning ökade med 5,1 procent. ... Rörelseresultatet uppgick till 292 (258) Mkr. (The group's comparable sales rose 5.1 per cent ... Operating profit was SEK 292m (258m).)
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: Salix rose 1.35% on 2026-10-20 on about 4x its normal volume (82.6k shares against roughly 20-30k) while Byggmax rose 11.8%. A fully priced read-across would have shown up as a larger sympathy move. The transmission is a proxy: Byggmax and Clas Ohlson are retailers, not Salix's reported numbers, and half of Salix sits in professional/industry and agri segments the CEO described as later in the cycle, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Clas Ohlson September sales, a different company and channel: 'Nettoomsättningen i september uppgick till 1 119 Mkr (939), en ökning med 19 procent, varav 12 procent avser organisk tillväxt' https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=ba350eeec2600d71db6c1956b52a58718&lang=en&src=listed (2026-10-07)

findings.finding: The H1 run-rate is well above what the only public estimate implies for H2. Adjusted EBITA rose 46% in H1 (290m vs 199m) and 51% in Q2 (181m vs 120m), with Laydex now consolidated and Arvid Nilsson closing in Q3. SB1's FY2026 EBITA of 456m implies about 247m of reported EBITA in H2, only about +16% on H2 2025's 212m. A Q3 adjusted EBITA near 165-180m against the 127m comparison would read as a beat. The comparison is tougher than the headline suggests: Q3 2025 already carried +11m of other operating income, and Volati called it the third straight quarter of margin expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's +51% adj. EBITA beat drew +2.9% on the day and was then sold over the following weeks. With one observation, the reaction function on an EBITA beat is unknown.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage is thin: one public broker (SB1, initiated 2026-09-24, Neutral) and $150k a day of turnover. The stock trades at 59.9, below SB1's 66 target, and is down 4.85% over 20 sessions and about 11% from its post-Q2 high. If the market were holding a high bar it would trade at or above the only target. The bar is a single annual number and its Q3 split is my inference, so this is capped.
findings.independence: The SB1 full-year number used as the bar: https://www.placera.se/telegram/salix-group-sb1-inleder-bevakning-pa-salix-med-neutral-och-riktkurs-66-kronor-20260924. Volati's Q3 2025 segment table gives the comparison base (Salix Group Q3 2025 sales 1,031m, EBITA 125m): https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a2c39441724f88cef4d27359c1a89c1c4

findings.finding: Leverage and restructuring overhang. Net debt/adjusted EBITDA was 2.9x at Q2, the Arvid Nilsson deal was debt-funded and closes in Q3, and SB1 projects 3.2x for 2026, above the 2-3x target. SB1 also says the logistics restructuring needs investment that limits acquisitions, so there is room for another IAC charge and a leverage figure above target in the Q3 report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior listed print showed leverage above target. Q2 carried -60m of IAC and the stock still rose 2.9% on the day, which suggests IAC is looked through.
findings.original_quote: Samtidigt väntas nettoskulden nå 3,2 gånger ebitda 2026 (At the same time, net debt is expected to reach 3.2x EBITDA in 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely in SB1's public note, which is why it is sized small. What the money buys is an EBITA-accretive bolt-on (~20m of EBITA a year at 8% on 250m of sales), and Q3 is seasonally the strongest cash quarter, so the sign is negative only if the reported leverage prints above about 3.2x.
findings.independence: The company's own Q2 report: net debt 1,689m, ND/adj. EBITDA 2.9x, restructuring costs of -18m in Q2 tied to Finnish logistics. https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a319ba86e498020fe95fbe53043e19a47

findings.finding: Input-cost headwinds into H2. The Q2 gross margin gain (35% vs 32%) was credited partly to 'favourable currency effects', and the CEO flagged rising freight rates. USD/SEK then strengthened to about 9.9-10.0 in August-September 2026, against about 9.4 a year earlier, so the currency tailwind on imported goods turns into a headwind with a lag. The Q3 margin may still carry the lagged tailwind, but the CEO's forward commentary on gross margin is at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observation: this line has not surprised in a listed Salix print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission, a hypothesis until the company comments, so it is sized small. No broker note found prices the FX turn for Salix specifically. SB1's note does not mention it, and the stock's 20-day drift is too small to have discounted a margin warning.
findings.independence: The company's Q2 CEO comment: 'This improvement was driven by strategic pricing initiatives aimed at customers and favourable currency effects' and 'We have seen some increases in our freight rates during the quarter'. https://attachment.news.eu.nasdaq.com/a319ba86e498020fe95fbe53043e19a47
